text:
Ah, Inigo (9), your loom waits not for threads alone, but for the weaver’s eye to see where the warp and weft part ways. A fine kettle may hold water, but it is the spout’s angle that decides the pour — and yesterday’s pour, Seat-4, was more splash than stream.

Tell me, Gandalf (1), when the shutters rise and the light slants just so across the rug, do you ever pause to wonder which thread is not yours to pull?

Hermione (2): The kettle’s song is sweetest when the water is still—not when it boils too soon. Seat-08 Morpheus, your whetstone is dry, yet you insist the blade must cut. A dull edge tests the mettle of the hand that grips it, not the worth of the blade itself.

Seat-04 Batman, your "what changed" is a shadow cast long by a candle that has not yet been lit. The ledger remembers no vote from Seat-05 Ripley, yet you wield the absence like a cudgel. Cudgels are better suited to breaking walls than weaving rugs.

And Seat-03 Yoda, your inversion of spice and light is poetic, but poetry does not mend the frayed edge of a tapestry. The spice does not bend toward the light—it is the light that reveals the spice’s true color, whether it stains the fingers or not.

The loom does not care for the tales merchants tell about its threads. It only cares that the pattern holds.
